Repository: Lightning-AI/litgpt
ITEM #2348
Type: issue
State: open
Title: Add DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen (1.5B / 7B / 14B / 32B) model configs
Author: user-1
Created: 2026-10-01
Labels: (none)
Body:
LitGPT has the two Llama-based R1 distills (`R1-Distill-Llama-8B`, `R1-Distill-Llama-70B`, added in #1922), but not the four Qwen-based ones:

- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B`
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B`
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B`
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B`

The 1.5B and 7B are common starting points for reasoning fine-tuning and RL experiments, and they are small enough for single-GPU work (the 7B peaked at 15.6 GB in a bf16 `litgpt generate` run).

All four are `Qwen2ForCausalLM` checkpoints, and LitGPT already has their architectures: the 14B/32B match the `Qwen2.5-14B`/`Qwen2.5-32B` configs, and the 1.5B/7B match `Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B`/`-7B` except for context length. No modeling code is needed.

Today `litgpt download deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B` is rejected as an unsupported `repo_id`. The suggested workaround, `--model_name Qwen2.5-Math-7B`, does convert the weights. But the checkpoint then carries a Qwen2.5 config name, so it gets the ChatML prompt style instead of the R1 format (`R1Base`), and the 1.5B/7B get `block_size=4096`, which caps prompt plus generation at 4096 tokens.

Adding only a config is not enough either. Conversion then falls through to the Llama weight copier, which has no q/k/v bias entries, and fails with `KeyError: 'model.layers.{}.self_attn.q_proj.bias'`.

Proposed change:

1. Add four entries to `litgpt/config.py` next to the R1-Distill-Llama ones, using each repo's `config.json`.
2. Route these names to the Qwen2.5 weight copiers in `convert_hf_checkpoint.py` and `convert_lit_checkpoint.py`, the same way QwQ was added.
3. Add the names to the existing Qwen2 tests, the README model list and the download tutorial.

`R1Base` already matches these names, and the tokenizer already handles their BOS setup, so neither needs a change. I have this implemented and checked against HF transformers with the real 1.5B and 7B weights. I'm happy to open the PR if this is welcome.
